subject: Is gl2gi correct for silicoDArT data?

messages.author: db110882830e3322
messages.subject: Is gl2gi correct for silicoDArT data?
parts:
Hullo,

Should we  be able to convert a silicoDArT genlight object to a genind using "gl2gi"? Applying "gl2gi" to the test set (and similarly to my own data), does the created genind object below look correct, or do we need to then "manually" change @ploidy and @call$ploidy from 2 to 1 and @type from codom to "P/A" before using the genind object for further analyses of the presence/ absence data?

Thanks for your advice,
Regards
Caroline.

test <- gl.read.silicodart(
  filename="testset_SilicoDArT.csv",
  ind.metafile="testset_metadata_silicodart.csv")

saveRDS(test, file="silicotest.rdata")
gitest <- gl2gi(test)

> test

/// GENLIGHT OBJECT /////////

 // 218 genotypes,  255 binary SNPs, size: 531.6 Kb

 2184 (3.93 %) missing data

 // Basic content

   @gen: list of 218 SNPbin

   @ploidy: ploidy of each individual  (range: 1-1)

 // Optional content

   @ind.names:  218 individual labels

   @loc.names:  255 locus labels

   @pop: population of each individual (group size range: 1-11)

   @other: a list containing: loc.metrics  latlong  ind.metrics  history  loc.metrics.flags  verbose

 

> gitest

/// GENIND OBJECT /////////

 // 218 individuals; 255 loci; 469 alleles; size: 728.7 Kb

 // Basic content

   @tab:  218 x 469 matrix of allele counts

   @loc.n.all: number of alleles per locus (range: 1-2)

   @loc.fac: locus factor for the 469 columns of @tab

   @all.names: list of allele names for each locus

   @ploidy: ploidy of each individual  (range: 2-2)

   @type:  codom

   @call: df2genind(X = xx[, ], sep = "/", ncode = 1, ind.names = g...@ind.names,

    pop = gl@pop, NA.char = "-", ploidy = 2)

 // Optional content

   @pop: population of each individual (group size range: 1-11)

   @other: a list containing: loc.metrics  latlong  ind.metrics  history  loc.metrics.flags  verbose
